{status: error, reason: conflict — checkpoint already resolved}

cards.title: Two options, not three (decision 95)
items: A third option — targeted re-run of Compliance Analyst on a single flagged item — was dropped for v1: nothing in the LangGraph shape supports partial re-invocation from the UI
"Accept as insufficient" appends a supervision_questions[] row; "human-asserted verdict" writes asserted_by: "human" so the audit trail never conflates a human call with a model call

cards.title: Concurrency guard (ADR-0018 §3) — the one mechanism common to every checkpoint
items: Every interrupt() carries a version/etag; a second resolution attempt on an already-resolved checkpoint is rejected with an explicit conflict, never silently overwritten or double-applied — this diagram is the first to draw that protocol, chosen here since Gap Analysis's two-option shape makes a stale-etag double-submit easy to illustrate concretely

Same protocol applies to every other checkpoint's interrupt() resolution (Setup, Intake, Supervision Sign-off, Findings, AG Feedback, Further-Submission) — not redrawn on each of those diagrams to avoid repeating an identical four-message block

cards.title: Diagram scope
items: "Analysis Complete" (decision 96) is a read of compliance_verdicts[] state, not a write — no separate sign-off call attests to anything the two resolution writes don't already determine
The citation-grounding call sequence that produces the initial flag is drawn in lfi-guardrail-citation-grounding-v1.html, not repeated here
